description: Mooring and unloading of tank barges of sulfuric acid and caustic soda; dock transfer pumps and emergency shutdown on the dock transfer PLC
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Barges can wait at the dock or anchorage; demurrage about $15,000 per day; acid and caustic tanks hold about 3 weeks of sales; transfers must not start without a working emergency shutdown
manual_workaround: Delay the barge; if a transfer is under way, stop it with the local emergency stop and manual valves; no transfer restarts until the dock transfer PLC and tank gauging are trusted
dependent_systems: SYS-04 (dock transfer PLC, tank gauging); SYS-01; SYS-06; SYS-17
dependent_third_parties: Barge operators; towing company; Captain of the Port (MTSA)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Terminal Manager (person in charge); terminal operators; FSO
quantified_operational_impact: Up to 2 barge receipts a week; a 72-hour delay holds 1 barge (about 10,000 barrels)
quantified_regulatory_impact: FSP and 33 CFR Part 154 transfer procedures must be followed; a breach of security or TSI concern is reported to the National Response Center (33 CFR 101.305)
process_safety_impact: Moderate: loss of emergency shutdown during a transfer could release acid or caustic to the dock or water
regulatory_linkage: 33 CFR Part 105 FSP; 33 CFR Part 154; 33 CFR 101.650 (critical OT)

business_process: Bulk tank farm, inventory control, and bulk resale
description: Tank gauging, transfers between tanks, inventory for 14 bulk tanks, and bulk resale of sulfuric acid and caustic soda
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Overfill protection depends on trusted level readings; bulk resale about $240,000 per shipping day; manual gauging is possible for one 12-hour shift with extra staff
manual_workaround: Stop all transfers; gauge tanks manually each shift; SIS high-level trips stay active; ship only from tanks with verified manual levels
dependent_people_or_facilities: Tank farm operators; Controls Engineering Manager
quantified_operational_impact: 14 bulk tanks; about 60 transfers a day; manual gauging needs 4 extra operators per shift
quantified_regulatory_impact: Release of sulfuric acid at or above 1,000 lb or sodium hypochlorite at or above 100 lb is reportable immediately (40 CFR 302.6)
process_safety_impact: Severe: overfill of a bulk tank if level readings are false

business_process: Ammonia Unit: anhydrous ammonia storage and aqua ammonia production
description: Rail unloading of anhydrous ammonia, storage, dilution to 19% and 29% aqua ammonia, product storage
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $260,000 of aqua ammonia shipments per day, mostly to water utilities that hold 3 to 5 days of supply; RMP Program 3 and PSM process; RPO 24 h matches the nightly online configuration export (offline copy weekly)
manual_workaround: Hold the unit in a safe state (isolated, no transfers); supply priority water utility customers from aqua ammonia already in storage (about 2 days); buy from a third-party supplier for longer outages
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-03; SYS-05; SYS-06; Port OT workstations (SYS-15)
dependent_third_parties: DCS integrator; SIS vendor; anhydrous ammonia supplier; rail carrier
dependent_people_or_facilities: Ammonia Unit operators; Shift Supervisors; Controls Engineering Manager; emergency response team
quantified_operational_impact: Produces about 40 tank truck loads of aqua ammonia a week
quantified_regulatory_impact: A release of 100 lb or more of ammonia is reportable immediately (40 CFR 302.6; 355.40); an RMP incident investigation must start within 48 hours (68.81(b)); RMP-reportable accident triggers 68.195 and 68.210
process_safety_impact: Severe: toxic release that can reach the public (worst-case endpoint reaches public receptors)
regulatory_linkage: 40 CFR Part 68 Program 3; 29 CFR 1910.119; 33 CFR 101.650 (critical OT)

business_process: Peroxide Unit: hydrogen peroxide storage and dilution
description: Receipt of 70% hydrogen peroxide, dilution to 50% and 35%, storage, and bulk loading
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $230,000 of peroxide shipments per day; pulp and paper customers hold about 4 days; PSM process; decomposition hazard if temperature or contamination controls fail
manual_workaround: Hold tanks in a safe state with temperature trips active; ship 50% product from storage; customers on allocation
dependent_third_parties: DCS integrator; SIS vendor; peroxide supplier
dependent_people_or_facilities: Peroxide Unit operators; Process Safety Manager
quantified_operational_impact: About 30 cargo tank loads a week
quantified_regulatory_impact: PSM incident investigation within 48 hours if a catastrophic release could have occurred (1910.119(m)); DOT security plan covers the 50% product in transport
process_safety_impact: Severe: runaway decomposition or overpressure if temperature or contamination controls fail
regulatory_linkage: 29 CFR 1910.119; 49 CFR 172.800; legacy CFATS chemical of interest

description: Batch execution of water treatment, pulp and paper, and sanitation formulations in 12 DCS-controlled blend reactors
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $420,000 of blended product shipments per day; about 55 batches a day; restart depends on a verified DCS configuration and master recipes
manual_workaround: Hold reactors in a safe state; run the 15 highest-volume formulations at the Inland plant (about 20% of Blend Hall 1 volume); allocate customers
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-05; SYS-06; Port OT workstations (SYS-15)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Blend operators; Shift Supervisors; Director of Technical Services
quantified_operational_impact: About 55 batches a day; a 24-hour stop loses about 1 day of Blend Hall 1 output
quantified_regulatory_impact: Product quality records must support certificates of analysis; deviations reviewed by the Quality Director
process_safety_impact: Moderate: an altered recipe can create an incompatible mixture

business_process: Process safety monitoring and emergency shutdown
description: SIS trips, ammonia and peroxide area gas and temperature detection, tank high-level protection, emergency shutdown valves
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Without verified SIS logic the Ammonia and Peroxide Units must stay isolated with portable detection and a standby watch; the Process Safety Manager limits this to one shift. RPO 0: the SIS logic must match the approved copy exactly
manual_workaround: Stop the Ammonia and Peroxide Units and all transfers; isolate with manual valves; portable detectors; standby watch under the emergency response plan
dependent_people_or_facilities: I&E technicians; Shift Supervisors; Process Safety Manager
quantified_operational_impact: Stopping the Ammonia Unit, Peroxide Unit, and Blend Hall 1 for 8 hours loses about one third of a day of Port production
quantified_regulatory_impact: SIS is an emergency shutdown system and control under mechanical integrity (68.73(a)(4)-(5); 1910.119(j)(1)(iv)-(v)); running without it is a deviation that needs MOC
process_safety_impact: Severe: loss of the last automated safeguard against a toxic release

description: Filling drums, totes, and pails on 5 PLC-controlled lines
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Finished goods cover about 2 days of packaged orders
manual_workaround: Manual filling on scales at reduced rate; pre-printed labels from the ERP
quantified_regulatory_impact: Hazard communication labels must stay accurate (29 CFR 1910.1200)

business_process: Bulk truck loading and rail shipping
description: 6 loading bays with metering, ground verification, driver card readers; rail loading of aqua ammonia
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 90 bulk truck loads a day; hazmat shipping papers come from the ERP; water utility deliveries cannot wait more than about 1 day
manual_workaround: Bays in local mode with two-person verification; pre-printed shipping papers; manual driver verification at the gate
dependent_people_or_facilities: Loading staff; Logistics Manager; gate security
quantified_operational_impact: About 90 truck loads a day; local mode cuts throughput by about half
quantified_regulatory_impact: Hazmat shipping papers must be accurate (49 CFR Part 172 Subpart C); DOT security plan measures for 50% peroxide (172.802)
process_safety_impact: Moderate: overfill or wrong product loaded if metering is bypassed

description: Sampling, lab testing, LIMS results, certificates of analysis, batch release for both plants
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No shipment leaves without a certificate of analysis; customers audit batch records
manual_workaround: Paper worksheets and typed certificates for up to 2 days
quantified_operational_impact: About 140 certificates a day across both plants
quantified_regulatory_impact: Certificates support customer specifications; water utility customers need product certifications on file

description: Emergency response team, community notification, calls to 911, the National Response Center, the SERC and LEPC; MTSA and cyber reporting
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Release notices are due immediately (40 CFR 302.6; 355.42-355.43); the emergency response plan must work when the business network is down; MTSA reports go without delay or immediately
manual_workaround: Printed call lists, radios, and cellular phones in the control room, gatehouse, and emergency response vehicle; satellite phone in the control room
dependent_systems: SYS-14 (phones and email); SYS-17; cellular service
dependent_third_parties: Cellular carrier; county fire rescue; LEPC
dependent_people_or_facilities: Emergency response team; Shift Supervisors; VP EHS and Process Safety; FSO
quantified_operational_impact: Must work within minutes on any shift
quantified_regulatory_impact: Late release notification is a violation of 40 CFR 302.6 and 355.40; RMP 68.95 emergency response program; FSP reporting duties
process_safety_impact: Severe: delayed community warning during a toxic release

description: FSP measures: access control and TWIC verification, cameras, gate control, dock security, declarations of security
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: FSP measures must stay in place at the current MARSEC level; camera and badge outages need extra guards within the shift
manual_workaround: Post guards at gates and the dock; visual TWIC checks; manual logs
quantified_regulatory_impact: FSP compliance; breaches of security are reported to the National Response Center without delay (33 CFR 101.305(b))
process_safety_impact: Moderate: theft or diversion of hydrogen peroxide if access control fails

description: PLC-controlled blending and packaging of cleaning, sanitation, and water treatment blends
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $360,000 of shipments per day; food plant sanitation customers hold about 1 week; restart depends on PLC programs held on one engineer's laptop
manual_workaround: Manual batching for the top 30 products at about 40% of normal rate; allocate customers
dependent_systems: SYS-08; SYS-09; SYS-10; SYS-15 (Inland OT workstations)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Inland operators; Inland Plant Manager; Inland controls engineer
quantified_operational_impact: About 30 batches and 25 truckloads a day
quantified_regulatory_impact: Hazard communication and product registration records
process_safety_impact: Moderate: incompatible mixture if a recipe or PLC program is altered

description: Warehouse picking, fleet dispatch for 30 cargo tank trucks, hazmat shipping papers, telematics
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 120 packaged and bulk deliveries a day; drivers need accurate shipping papers and route plans
manual_workaround: Paper dispatch sheets; drivers call in; pre-printed shipping papers from the last ERP extract
dependent_third_parties: Fleet management SaaS vendor; contract carriers
quantified_operational_impact: 30 company trucks and about 40 contract carrier loads a day
quantified_regulatory_impact: Hazmat shipping papers (49 CFR Part 172 Subpart C); en route security measures in the DOT security plan (172.802(a)(3))
process_safety_impact: Moderate: misrouted or mis-documented hazmat load

business_process: TTRS telemetry monitoring and automatic replenishment
description: Telemetry from 420 customer tanks, customer portal, replenishment engine and AI-004 forecasts that create ERP orders
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Contract commits 99.5% monthly availability and replenishment orders within 4 hours of a reorder point; water utilities rely on it for treatment chemicals; TTRS drives about $300,000 of orders per day and earns about $18,000 per day in service fees
manual_workaround: Customer service calls the 160 water utility sites daily and takes tank readings by phone; dispatch from the last known levels plus a safety margin
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider; cellular carrier; ERP vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Customer Solutions team; customer service; dispatch
quantified_operational_impact: 420 monitored tanks; about 70 automatic orders a day
quantified_regulatory_impact: Contract service credits; water utility customers may face treatment chemical shortages (their own regulatory exposure)
process_safety_impact: Moderate: a water utility running out of treatment chemical

description: Customer orders, credit holds, pricing, delivery scheduling, and customer service in the ERP
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $1.64 million of orders per shipping day flow through the ERP; most are recoverable within a week but spot orders are lost
manual_workaround: Phone and paper orders from the last ERP extract; priority list of water utility and food plant customers

description: Master recipes in the batch management system, bills of materials and formulations in the ERP, recipe release workflow
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Recipes are needed to restart BP-05 and BP-12; about 900 formulations are trade secrets; an altered recipe can create an incompatible mixture
manual_workaround: Printed recipe cards for the top 60 formulations in each control room; ERP bills of materials as a cross-check
dependent_people_or_facilities: Director of Technical Services; Quality Director
quantified_operational_impact: About 900 formulations; about 25 recipe changes a month
quantified_regulatory_impact: Formulation changes for registered products need regulatory review
process_safety_impact: Moderate: incompatible mixture from an altered recipe

description: Raw material purchasing, supplier payments, customer invoicing and collections
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cash flow; supplier terms allow short delays; bank portal is separate
manual_workaround: Phone orders to key suppliers; invoices queued in the ERP
quantified_operational_impact: About $8 million of receivables collected per week

description: Time capture, payroll, onboarding, terminations, TWIC sponsorship
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly; terminations must still remove access the same day
manual_workaround: Repeat prior payroll through the provider; manual termination checklist including OT accounts and driver cards
quantified_regulatory_impact: Wage payment timing under state law; access removal at termination (33 CFR 101.650(a)(7))
